activity.overview: Use a timeline to understand the major events of the Cold War and the decades since, and connect them to earlier units.

problems.prompt: What was containment? Name two policies from 1947 that put it into practice.
Name two times the Cold War became a shooting war involving American troops, and one time it nearly became a nuclear war.
How did the Cold War affect civil liberties at home in the early 1950s? Connect your answer to a case or law from Unit 5.
List, in order, the three events of 1989-1991 that ended the Cold War.
What law did Congress pass after the attacks of September 11, 2001, and what earlier unit does it remind you of? Explain the connection.
Choose one event on the timeline that changed American life at home, not only foreign policy, and explain how.

activity.subject: history-social-studies
activity.title: The Cold War in Twelve Events

readings.body:
1945: The Second World War ends. The United States and the Soviet Union emerge as rival superpowers; Europe is divided between them.
1947: President Truman asks Congress for aid to Greece and Turkey, announcing the Truman Doctrine. The Marshall Plan for European recovery follows.
1948-1949: The Soviet Union blockades West Berlin; the United States and Britain supply the city by air for nearly a year. The NATO alliance forms in 1949, the year the Soviet Union tests its first atomic bomb.
1950-1953: The Korean War. The fighting ends in an armistice near the line where it began.
Early 1950s: Senator Joseph McCarthy's accusations of communist infiltration feed a Red Scare in which many Americans lose jobs over their political associations.
1957: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik, the first artificial satellite. Congress responds with new spending on science education.
1961: President Eisenhower's farewell address in January. The Berlin Wall goes up in August.
1962: The Cuban Missile Crisis brings the superpowers close to nuclear war.
1964-1973: After the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution in 1964, American involvement in the Vietnam War grows to more than half a million troops. Protests divide the country. American combat forces leave in 1973; Saigon falls in 1975.
1974: Facing impeachment over the Watergate scandal, President Richard Nixon resigns.
1987: President Ronald Reagan speaks at the Berlin Wall. Later that year he and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev sign a treaty eliminating a whole class of nuclear missiles.
1989-1991: The Berlin Wall falls in November 1989. Germany reunites in 1990. The Soviet Union dissolves in December 1991.
2001: Terrorists kill nearly 3,000 people on September 11. Congress passes the USA PATRIOT Act, expanding government surveillance powers, and the United States goes to war in Afghanistan.
2008: A financial crisis sets off the Great Recession, the deepest economic downturn since the 1930s.
readings.title: The Cold War and After, 1945-2008: A Timeline
